gap: No result ChatGPT got states how much power a small 2-bay NAS actually draws (Synology rates the DS225+ at 16.98 W in use and 6.08 W with drives asleep) or how many minutes a small UPS lasts at that load. Without both, nobody can say whether a 600 VA unit covers the wait plus a clean shutdown.
standout_why: I compared HoldBackup (cited), RacksAndWatts and TechFromAlex. HoldBackup gives a CyberPower figure for the CP1500PFCLCD (66 min at 100 W) but only a made-up 60 W NAS draw, which it says was not measured. RacksAndWatts has no runtimes and no NAS power figures, only made-up worksheet hosts. TechFromAlex gives only a 3-minute full-load runtime for the CP850PFCLCD and no NAS power draw. ChatGPT's answer says 600–900 VA is 'usually enough' with no load or runtime figures. A real 2-bay NAS draw is new. I could not open any small-UPS runtime-at-low-load figure, so this is a 2 and not a 3.
decides: A 2-bay NAS at about 17 W in use takes 5.1% of the BE600M1's 330 W rating. The VA rating doesn't limit the choice; runtime at low load and a working shutdown signal do. That supports the smallest UPS that is on the NAS maker's compatibility list (BE600M1 or similar), and it means the 850 VA picks buy headroom a 2-bay NAS doesn't need. The runtime-per-candidate column could not be filled from pages I could open, so it does not yet rank the candidates by minutes.
